short: The field of AI focused on enabling machines to interpret, understand, and extract meaning from images and video.
eli5: Giving computers eyes and visual common sense so pixels turn into recognizable objects and scenes.
example: Autonomous vehicles spotting pedestrians, lane markings, and traffic signs in camera feeds.

short: A neural architecture using sliding local filters to detect spatial hierarchies from edges up to whole objects.
eli5: Scanning a photo with tiny magnifying glasses—first spotting lines and corners, then eyes and ears, then a cat.
example: ResNet architectures classifying thousands of wildlife photos from camera traps.

short: Sliding a small learnable weight kernel across an image grid to compute local responses like edges, textures, or blobs.
eli5: Stamping a small stencil across every patch of a picture to measure where a certain pattern shows up.
example: A 3x3 vertical edge filter lighting up strongly along building pillars.

short: A downsampling step that summarizes small patches of a feature map (e.g., taking the max value) to shrink size and add shift tolerance.
eli5: Zooming out on a mosaic by keeping only the brightest tile in every 2x2 square.
example: 2x2 max pooling halving image width and height between convolutional blocks.

short: Predicting a single category label that describes the primary subject of an entire image.
eli5: Looking at a photo and putting one sticker on it: 'golden retriever' or 'espresso'.
example: Sorting uploaded user photos into plant species categories.

short: Simultaneously identifying what objects appear in an image and locating each one with a tight bounding box.
eli5: Both naming every item in a room and drawing a neat rectangle around where each one sits.
example: Warehouse cameras counting and boxing pallets, forklifts, and safety vests in real time.

short: Assigning a class label to every individual pixel in an image to trace exact object boundaries.
eli5: Coloring a photo like a precise coloring book where every road pixel is gray and every tree pixel is green.
example: Separating satellite imagery pixel-by-pixel into forest, water, farmland, and buildings.

short: An image architecture that splits an image into square patches and feeds them as visual tokens into a Transformer.
eli5: Cutting a photo into a grid of puzzle squares and letting a Transformer read them like words in a sentence.
example: Powering multimodal models that jointly reason over screenshots and user questions.

short: The 2D grid of activations produced when a convolutional filter slides across an image, showing where a pattern was detected.
eli5: A heatmap tracing everywhere a specific shape—like curved whiskers or brick textures—appeared in the photo.
example: Early layers yielding sharp edge maps while deep layers highlight wheel or face regions.

short: Artificially expanding training data by applying realistic flips, crops, rotations, or color shifts that preserve the true label.
eli5: Practicing recognizing a friend from tilted, sunny, and shadowed photos so you still know them in bad lighting.
example: Horizontally flipping street-view photos during training to double dataset diversity without relabeling.

short: A rectangular coordinate frame [x, y, width, height] marking the spatial location of a detected object.
eli5: The tight imaginary box drawn around an object so a computer knows exactly where it begins and ends.
example: Outputting [120, 80, 210, 340] for a bicycle detected on a crosswalk.

short: Converting photographed, scanned, or handwritten text inside images into editable machine-readable strings.
eli5: Looking at a photo of a paper receipt and typing every word and price into a spreadsheet automatically.
example: Digitizing street signs, license plates, and scanned PDF invoices.
